evidence: New persisted families without an explicit parentPin are unconfigured and generate no console PIN; restart and a later deployment PIN do not override the saved status.
All eight existing public actions work before setup, while protected writes and challenges require PARENT_SETUP_REQUIRED.
parent.setup accepts only its declared fields; first PIN is six ASCII digits with identical confirmation; math accepts no PIN fields and creates no hidden credentials.
A setup writes configuration, one action ID and one salted scrypt receipt without changing business ledgers; the original business operation still needs the ordinary challenge and grant.
Different concurrent setups produce one success and one PARENT_ALREADY_CONFIGURED conflict; identical concurrent retries produce one durable commit.
Exact setup retries work after restart and later writes; changed PIN or confirmation under the same ID is rejected.
A public write can stale a setup while keeping initialization open; retry with the latest revision preserves the public write.
A forced atomic file write failure leaves credentials, revision, action IDs and receipts unchanged, and the identical request can retry successfully.
Self-set PIN changes require the current credential and validate supplied confirmation; first math can switch to a new PIN only after the current arithmetic challenge.
Legacy pin and math configurations without the configured marker retain state, receipts and credential hashes, including twelve-digit PIN verification; they never reopen public setup.
Malformed configured flags, credential pairs, legacy empty math credentials and unset state with prior sensitive receipts fail closed without rewriting the source file.
Same-origin protection rejects cross-origin first setup; public metadata and snapshots expose only configured and method, with revision available for ordering.
